answer: Funding-lineage panel exclusion stops a farm from grading its own seats. Each seat's first coins are traced back three hops, and seats drawing over 20% of their funds from a shared source wallet form one lineage that never sits twice on a 5-grader panel. So when an answer about planting willow along a canyon terrace is judged, at most one grader from any ring scores it. Fifty fakes funded by one wallet buy one panel vote, not fifty; each extra colluding vote needs its own earned history of about 6 passed epochs, and relay wallets fail because they inherit the source's lineage.
